items.prompt:
When a text deliberately leaves its meaning open, it is:
A) ambiguous
B) a summary
C) a title

'Strong' textual evidence is the:
A) most convincing evidence
B) longest sentence
C) first word

An inference is a conclusion drawn from:
A) evidence and reasoning
B) a guess
C) the title

Read.

He assured the board that 'nothing was wrong,' then shredded the files that night.

The strongest evidence shows he was:
A) honest and calm
B) hiding wrongdoing
C) celebrating

steps: Shredding at night. Key is B.

items.prompt:
A novel ends as a character opens a door 'onto darkness,' revealing nothing beyond. The author has:
A) deliberately left the outcome uncertain
B) made an error
C) resolved the plot fully
items.answer: A) deliberately left the outcome uncertain

solution.answer: A) deliberately left the outcome uncertain

items.prompt:
'Strong AND thorough' evidence means it is:
A) the most convincing, and there is enough of it
B) a single weak detail
C) unrelated to the claim
items.answer: A) the most convincing, and there is enough of it

solution.answer: A) the most convincing, and there is enough of it

items.prompt:
Why might an author deliberately leave a key matter UNCERTAIN at a story's end?
A) to invite interpretation and reflect life's real uncertainty
B) because they forgot to finish
C) to avoid having any meaning
items.answer: A) to invite interpretation and reflect life's real uncertainty

solution.answer: A) to invite interpretation and reflect life's real uncertainty

items.prompt:
Which is the WEAKEST evidence that a character is secretly afraid?
A) 'He checked the locks three times and slept with the light on.'
B) 'He owns a brown briefcase.'
C) 'He startled at every sound.'

steps: Irrelevant to fear. Key is B.
